plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers atop sturdy stems and broad blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist in nearly every color and form, from single and double blooms to fringed and parrot types.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to early May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated across temperate regions, especially the Netherlands, North America, and Europe; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the 17th-century Dutch 'Tulip Mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Prunus serrulata
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree that bursts into clouds of blossoms before or as the leaves emerge. Late-blooming cultivars such as 'Kanzan' produce dense, double pink flowers in mid to late April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (late-blooming varieties peak in mid-April)
plants.location: Japan, Korea, and China; widely planted in Washington D.C., Vancouver, and across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: In northern Japan, such as Hokkaido, cherry blossom season arrives in late April to early May, weeks after Tokyo, so the blossom 'front' moves north through the spring.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of pea-like flowers emerge directly from bare branches and even the trunk before the heart-shaped leaves appear. It is a valuable early nectar source for native bees.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from southern Ontario to northern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud blooms are edible and have a mild, slightly tart flavor; they are sometimes added to salads or used as garnishes.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing tree with fern-like foliage that produces masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. When blooming, the tree can look like a purple cloud and carpets the ground below with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (Sept to Dec); also blooms in autumn in some tropical and subtropical areas, with some trees flowering in April in parts of Northern Hemisphere warm climates and sporadically in the tropics
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa, Australia, Mexico, and California
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
